analogy: Wine becoming vinegar and broader transformation
premise: The primary sources attach consequences to a sufficiently changed substance, with authority-specific exceptions.
reasoning: A cultivated process must demonstrate what changes in each input and final material before transformation can be invoked.
counter_evidence: Cell proliferation is described as production of chicken cells in SFA and company records. Growth and a new commercial name do not by themselves demonstrate the required change of identity.
missing_test: A named authority must assess a chemically and biologically specified process against its own criterion.
verification_scope: Premises and limits checked; analogy remains an inference, not an attributed product ruling.

premise: IIFA210 treats source and slaughter as relevant to extracted rennet, records disagreement on unslaughtered sources, and allows genetically engineered rennet. Sistani distinguishes some extracted-material cases.
reasoning: An enzyme input should be traced to its production route; identical function does not establish identical source treatment.
counter_evidence: Rennet is an input, whereas harvested cultivated cells are the intended food biomass. A rennet permission cannot settle founder-cell status.
missing_test: Supplier provenance, fermentation host, substrate, processing aid and residual evidence for the particular enzyme.
verification_scope: Premises and limits checked; analogy remains an inference, not an attributed product ruling.

premise: IIFA198 allowed plasma on a transformation rationale, but210 reopened the issue. The GOOD dossier describes serum use and measurable residual albumin.
reasoning: Washing and safety tests address removal and exposure, not automatically religious transformation. Serum-containing and serum-free processes must remain separate.
counter_evidence: A low residue is not evidence of no residue or a universally accepted dilution rule. Plasma and serum are not interchangeable categories.
missing_test: All media stages, residual assays, detection limits and a specific authority’s removal/transformation criteria.
verification_scope: Premises and limits checked; analogy remains an inference, not an attributed product ruling.

analogy: Detached living flesh and egg-derived cells
premise: Classical texts classify detached living flesh; contemporary documents distinguish source routes, and SFA describes an embryonic stem-cell process.
reasoning: Donor procurement, original sample, founder line and later biomass are distinct objects of analysis. Compare a live biopsy with post-slaughter and egg-derived routes.
counter_evidence: A classical gross-tissue rule does not explicitly name a microscopic immortalized line. IIFA’s living-donor wording and MUIS’s egg discussion prevent silently imposing one route on every authority.
missing_test: Document founder-cell origin and explain why the classical legal category extends or does not extend to the defined modern object.
verification_scope: Premises and limits checked; analogy remains an inference, not an attributed product ruling.
